items.item: The form is split into titled sections (personal, job and contract, bank and tax, emergency contact, documents) in a single column, with a visible label above every field and no placeholder-only labels
items.evidence: Five <section> blocks each with an <h2>: 'Personal details', 'Job and contract', 'Bank and tax information', 'Emergency contact', 'Documents' (lines 80, 167, 246, 297, 336), stacked vertically inside a single max-w-3xl column. Every input/select has a <label class="block" for="..."> above it (e.g. <label for="firstName">First name *</label>). Placeholders like 'Minh Anh' or 'name@email.com' are supplementary example text, not substitutes for labels.

items.item: Required fields are marked consistently, and optional fields are labelled as optional or left unmarked by a stated convention
items.evidence:
Top-of-form legend '

* Required

' (line 71) establishes the convention; every required input/select carries a red '*' span (e.g. firstName, dob, bankName). The two optional fields, postalCode and ecEmail, have plain labels with no asterisk, consistent with the stated convention. Document items also append ' *' only when `doc.required` is true and show an explicit 'Optional' badge otherwise (renderDocuments(), lines 519-538).

items.item: Field widths match their content: dates, postal codes and tax codes are narrow; inputs use the right types (email, tel, date)
items.evidence: dob/startDate/contractEndDate use type="date" with class 'w-40' (160px); postalCode uses 'w-28' (112px) vs. free-text fields like address/jobTitle/accountHolder which use 'max-w-xl w-full' (up to 576px). taxCode/accountNumber use 'w-56' with inputmode="numeric" and tabular-nums — narrower than the full-width text fields though not as tight as postal code. personalEmail/ecEmail use type="email", phone/ecPhone use type="tel".

items.item: An option to save the form as a draft is offered, and saving a draft does not demand every required field
items.evidence: Sticky bar button id="draftBtn" labelled 'Save draft' (line 355). Its click handler (lines 651-660) only updates the draft indicator and shows a toast — it never calls validateField/FIELDS validation, so an incomplete form can be saved as a draft.

items.item: Save and Cancel stay reachable while scrolling (a sticky bar or equivalent), Save is a verb label and is not disabled before submitting
items.evidence: `<main id="scroll-main" class="h-[calc(100vh-73px)] overflow-y-auto">` is the sole scrolling ancestor (comment at line 67: 'the only scrolling ancestor, so the bottom bar can stick'); the action bar `<div class="sticky bottom-0 ...">` (line 350) sits outside it and stays visible. Save button text is 'Onboard employee' (verb phrase, line 361) and has no `disabled` attribute in markup — it's only set during submit (saveBtn.disabled = true at line 689) and cleared after.

items.item: Fields validate on blur and on submit; with several errors a summary at the top links to each field and focus moves to the first invalid field
items.evidence: blur listener calls runFieldValidation(name, true) (line 478); saveBtn click handler validates all FIELDS plus documents (lines 667-674). renderErrorSummary() builds a linked list of errors ('#${name}' anchors that call focusFirst on click) once entries.length >= 3 (lines 600-627). On submit, `focusFirst([firstInvalid[0]])` moves focus+scrolls to the first invalid field (lines 677-684).

items.item: Leaving the page with unsaved input triggers a warning
items.evidence: `window.addEventListener('beforeunload', ...)` calls `e.preventDefault()`/sets `e.returnValue` when `isDirty` (lines 593-597); Cancel button also opens a custom alertdialog ('You have unsaved changes. Leave without saving?', lines 367-376) when isDirty is true (lines 709-717).

items.item: The document upload states accepted file types and the size limit, lists chosen files with a remove button, and is keyboard operable
items.evidence: Documents section intro only reads 'Upload the documents required before the first day' (line 338) — no accepted file types or size limit are stated anywhere, and the hidden `<input type="file" id="fileInput" multiple>` (line 343) has no `accept` attribute and is never wired to any event listener; the visible 'Upload' button just fabricates a fake docState entry instead of opening a file picker (lines 561-571). Uploaded rows do show file name/size with a 'Remove' button (aria-label set, native <button>, keyboard operable), but the missing type/size disclosure fails this item.

items.item: Success is confirmed with a message that names the employee and is announced to assistive technology
items.evidence: On successful submit: `showToast(`Employee ${fullName} onboarded`)` (line 704) where fullName is built from firstName+lastName values; the toast container has `role="status"` (line 379), making it an assistive-tech live region.

notes: No template tells from the given list were observed: no greeting-header, no KPI tiles, no delta pills, no avatars, no gradients/glass effects, no uppercase tracked labels, no emoji icons (grep for emoji code points found none), status badges use plain semantic success/warning/neutral colors (not a 'rainbow' palette), no sidebar at all (so no sidebar-promo-card or navy-sidebar-indigo-accent), no decorative charts, no nested card-in-card structures, no hover-lift animations, and borderRadius tokens are capped at 8px (not oversized). The one functional gap is the document upload: it never discloses accepted file types/size limits and the real <input type="file"> is dead code — 'Upload' just mocks a successful upload rather than opening a file picker.
